title: 2026 401(k) elective deferral + catch-up limits (IRS join)
description: 2026 IRS join: $24,500 elective deferral, $8,000 age-50 catch-up, $11,250 ages 60–63, SIMPLE and 415(c) alongside. From Notice 2025-67. Not tax advice.
extract: For 2026, IRS Notice 2025-67 (IRB 2025-49) sets the section 402(g) elective-deferral limit at $24,500 (up from $23,500). The age-50 catch-up under section 414(v)(2)(B)(i) for plans other than SIMPLE 401(k)/SIMPLE IRA is $8,000. SECURE 2.0’s higher catch-up for employees who turn 60, 61, 62, or 63 in the calendar year is $11,250 for 2026. Combined employee elective deferrals plus catch-up are therefore $32,500 (age 50–59 or 64+) or $35,750 (age 60–63), unless the plan’s own limit is lower. Catch-up is not counted until deferrals exceed the $24,500 limit, the ADP test limit, or the plan limit. SIMPLE 401(k) uses a separate 2026 deferral of $17,000 and catch-up of $4,000 ($5,250 at ages 60–63). The section 415(c) annual-addition limit is $72,000; the compensation cap is $360,000. Beginning in 2026, if prior-year FICA wages from the plan sponsor exceeded $150,000, catch-up to a plan that offers Roth must be Roth. This page joins those IRS figures on one table. Compiled 2026-08-29. Not tax advice. Confirm with the plan document and a tax professional.

faq.q: What is the 2026 401(k) elective deferral limit?
faq.a: IRS Notice 2025-67 sets the 2026 section 402(g) elective-deferral limit at $24,500.

faq.q: What is the 2026 401(k) catch-up for age 50 versus ages 60–63?
faq.a: Age 50+ catch-up is $8,000. Employees turning 60, 61, 62, or 63 in 2026 may use $11,250. Combined with the $24,500 deferral that is $32,500 or $35,750 unless the plan is lower.

faq.q: When must 2026 catch-up contributions be Roth?
faq.a: If prior-year FICA wages from the plan sponsor exceeded $150,000, catch-up to a plan that offers Roth must be Roth beginning in 2026.
